set.body:
Raised by independent review of the new relation_fit, aimed at Epic 5 before residual streaming is built.

Observation

residual_block() results depend on the feature-block partition used to read them. Reassembling the full residual matrix from blocks of size 1/2/3/4/6 never reproduces the single-read result bitwise:

  block= 1  identical=FALSE  max|diff|=8.88e-16
  block= 2  identical=FALSE  max|diff|=2.22e-16
  block= 3  identical=FALSE  max|diff|=4.44e-16
  block= 4  identical=FALSE  max|diff|=2.22e-16
  block= 6  identical=FALSE  max|diff|=2.22e-16

This is 0.5-4 ULP - ordinary BLAS non-associativity across differently shaped column subsets, not a computational error.

Why it still needs a decision now

Epic 5 accumulates residual cross-products "over the union pair graph in bounded blocks". So the block plan - which is chosen from a memory budget - perturbs Sigma_hat, and Sigma_hat is inverted to produce the metric. The perturbation is amplified by the conditioning:

  fixture: n=80, p=40 correlated features, cond(Sigma) = 1.68e5
  Sigma relative diff, block=1 vs single read : 1.99e-16
  after inversion, K relative diff:
    lambda=0      cond=1.68e5   1.74e-12
    lambda=1e-6   cond=1.66e5   1.20e-12
    lambda=1e-3   cond=3.46e4   2.41e-13
    lambda=1e-2   cond=1.05e4   1.47e-14
    lambda=1e-1   cond=1.77e3   1.58e-15

Amplification tracks the condition number, roughly 1e4 here. Unshrunk local searchlight covariance at k~100 voxels and n~200 observations routinely reaches cond >= 1e8, which would put K at ~1e-8 relative - at or past the default expect_equal tolerance of 1.5e-8. A block-invariance test written against K could then fail for reasons unrelated to correctness.

Why this is a contract question rather than a defect

The package already commits to deterministic sequential execution and carries .canonical_reduce for radix-ordered bitwise-deterministic summation, and the effect-form kernel is tested for feature_block invariance. The metric path currently has no equivalent guarantee, so results would depend on the memory budget.

Two acceptable resolutions, but pick one deliberately

(a) Make residual accumulation canonical: fix a feature ordering and reduce with the existing .canonical_reduce machinery so Sigma_hat is bitwise identical regardless of block plan. Preferred - it preserves the guarantee that already exists elsewhere.
(b) State explicitly that metric construction is block-plan dependent to within a declared tolerance, record the block plan in the metric recipe signature so the same plan reproduces, and write the invariance tests on Sigma_hat with a stated tolerance rather than on K.

Verified correct in the same pass, no action needed
- residual_df = n - rank exactly (55 for n=60, rank 5).
- effect_covariance matches C (Xw^T Xw)^-1 C^T to 1.4e-17 with a nonidentity whitener.
- residual_block matches qr.resid(qr(LX), LY) to 1.4e-15; residuals orthogonal to the whitened design to 1.1e-14.
- Subset reads match the corresponding columns of a full read to 1.1e-16, in forward and reversed feature order.
- Capability refusal is exact: a relation_fit with no error channel reports all eight capabilities FALSE and refuses residual_block, effect_covariance and residual_df with precise messages naming the missing capability.
- A rank-deficient design is refused with "Requested effects are not estimable: e1" rather than silently returning a projected answer.
set.title: Residual blocks are not block-plan invariant; 1-ULP drift is amplified by metric inversion
